brief:
Arab-majority electoral lists are preparing to join an opposition alliance ahead of Israel's elections next week, according to Al-Monitor. The parties will not lead a government but could determine the outcome in a closely contested race, as their voter base seeks to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The strategy reflects growing frustration among Arab-Israeli voters with Netanyahu's tenure and their potential leverage in a fragmented political landscape where no single faction commands a majority.
dek: They will not govern Israel, but Arab-majority lists could be the kingmakers in Israel's close-fought elections next week, guided by a voter base fed up with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
title: Arab-Israeli parties position as kingmakers against Netanyahu
